Her story

Twenty years in, and still saying yes.

“

This opportunity arose to rejoin YWAM for a short period of time, and I'm pleased to be able to bring my wealth of experience and knowledge to support the new leadership of the San Francisco location.

Ange spent more than two decades with Youth With A Mission before stepping back. Now she's heading into San Francisco's Tenderloin for a defined season. Not to lead from the front, but to help build the infrastructure underneath a new generation of YWAM SF leadership as they grow their reach among the neighborhood's unhoused community.

It's practical work behind the scenes: the kind of scaffolding that lets a ministry serve more people, more sustainably. When you give, you're not just funding a program. You're putting Ange's gifts and years of experience directly to work for San Francisco's unhoused neighbors.

The ministry

What YWAM SF does in the Tenderloin

Free showers, hot meals, activities, pop-up church, and discipleship programs work together to create a safe community: a place where unhoused neighbors can find respite, belonging, and practical help.

The Ellis Room

When it rains, the lights stay on. Overnight, the Ellis Room becomes a dry, safe place for neighbors with nowhere else to go.

Meals

Hot meals cooked and served right on the block, including a Christmas Day lunch that reached over 200 neighbors.

Food Pantry

Every week, neighbors line up not just for groceries, but to be seen and known. Fresh produce, warm smiles, and no judgment.

Showers & practical care

Free showers, haircuts, toiletries, and everyday necessities. Dignity in the basics.

Pop-up church

Worship and a simple message, right on the sidewalk or tucked in a garden alley. Meeting people exactly where they are.

Discipleship

Ongoing discipleship programs that walk alongside neighbors and students for the long term, not just the moment.

Community & activities

Games, art, and conversation that build real belonging in the neighborhood.

Fellowship

Shared meals and shared tables. Where conversation turns into friendship, one lunch at a time.

Every week, they come

From above, the line tells its own story. Hundreds of neighbors, every week, trusting this block to show up for them.
